processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five Cu molds moved stepwise inside the furnace were successively filled from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.
10 × 50 × 130 mm³ blocks were hot rolled into 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets.
Scales were removed from the surfaces by low-pressure, fine-grit sandblasting after the heat treatments.
Samples for mechanical testing and microstructure investigation were prepared from the segments by package spark erosion.

structures.overall_structure: Single-phase austenitic (SIMPLEX) microstructure; fully recrystallized with ~20 µm grain size and some retained Mn microsegregations; no cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in the final material.

phases_present.morphology: single-phase austenite prevailing at room temperature; fully recrystallized

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: values plotted represent averages of three measurements for every material state

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; averages of three measurements per material state
characterization_methods.purpose: Mechanical property screening (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, total elongation)
characterization_methods.key_findings: For Fe-30Mn-1.2C-2Al aged 450 °C/1 h, YS ~350–450 MPa (Fig. 3a); tensile strength ~460–600 MPa and elongation ~8–55% (Fig. 4, 2Al cluster).

characterization_methods.purpose: Hardness screening of the aged RAP samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: Hardness nearly flat around 200 HBW over 0–6 wt.% Al, including the 2Al condition.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: grinding and polishing with standard metallographic techniques
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: cross-sectional areas prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction
characterization_methods.purpose: Microstructure inspection (cracks, pores, macrosegregations, grain structure)
characterization_methods.key_findings: No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in the final materials; fully recrystallized microstructure with ~20 µm grain size and some retained Mn microsegregations.

unmapped_findings: For the intermediate-Al alloy Fe-30Mn-1.2C-2Al (2 wt.% Al), aging has a much smaller influence on tensile behavior than for the Al-free alloy (weakening/embrittlement) and the 8 wt.% Al alloy (strengthening); its properties fall between the 0Al and 8Al behaviors [b0024, b0025].
With 30 wt.% Mn and 2 wt.% Al (≤4–5 wt.% Al), the TWIP effect prevails as the deformation mechanism, placing this sample in the SIMPLEX (single-phase austenitic TWIP) steel class [b0031].

Pronounced j-carbide (κ-carbide) formation/strengthening is associated in the paper with aging at 500–600 °C or with higher Al content (Al > 10 wt.% forming during quenching); the 450 °C/1 h, 2 wt.% Al condition of this sample is outside that stated regime [b0031, b0109].

Fig. 3 presents mechanical data for 45 material conditions of the Fe-30Mn-1.2C base composition; the 450 °C/1 h aging condition is drawn as the blue curve, but no printed per-condition numeric values at 2 wt.% Al are given in the text (only axis-level approximate ranges) [b0022, figure_003].
